priorFindingsResolution.note: self-fix.sh:13-17 now defines sf_pane_fingerprint(), which strips ALL digits and the literal 'esc to interrupt' (sed), strips a specific spinner-glyph set '✻✳✶✢⏺◐◓◑◒·↑↓…' (tr -d), and drops entire lines containing the word 'tokens' (grep -avE) BEFORE cksum. Hand-traced against the exact round-6 counterexample fixtures ('✻ Brewed for 3m · esc to interrupt', '✢ Searching… (7m · ↓ 19k tokens · esc to interrupt)') and the builder's new test-self-fix.sh:19-23 fixtures: a genuinely frozen fixer whose only change between checks is the elapsed-time/token-count status line now produces an IDENTICAL fingerprint (that whole status line is dropped wholesale by the 'tokens' line-filter, and any leftover digits elsewhere are stripped), while a fixer that emits genuinely new substantive text (a new tool call, new reasoning) produces a DIFFERENT fingerprint because that text is not digits/spinner-glyphs/a-tokens-line. The 180min kill ceiling (self-fix.sh:32,40) can now actually fire against the realistic hang class (stuck browser/network call with a ticking CLI status line) that defeated the round-6 patch. Residual, non-blocking caveat: the tr -d spinner-glyph set (✻✳✶✢⏺◐◓◑◒) is a fixed enumeration, not a class-based strip (e.g. not '[[:^ascii:]]' or a documented exhaustive Braille-spinner range); if the real Claude Code CLI ever renders a distinct spinner glyph outside this set on its ticking status line, that glyph would survive the strip and could defeat frozen-detection again. Grepped the entire skills/self tree for every other spinner/status-line fixture in this codebase (test-healthcheck-lib.sh, test-self-fix.sh) and found no glyph outside the covered set, so there is no on-disk evidence of an actual gap -- but this cannot be proven exhaustively without a live CLI capture, which is outside this review's evidence base. Recorded as a non-blocking note, not a finding, because it is unprovable speculation rather than a demonstrated defect.

finalAssessment.decisiveQuestion: Is the system NOW sound to run unattended (self-heal + self-improve + honest verification, no human, no permanent-disable path, no success-without-real-side-effect, a hang that IS eventually killed)?
finalAssessment.answer: NOT YET -- one genuine coverage gap remains, but the two critical/major mechanisms this round targeted are otherwise soundly fixed.
finalAssessment.summary: Genuine, disk-verified progress this round on both open critical/major items: FIND-029 (the CLI's ticking elapsed-time/token-counter status line defeating hang detection) is RESOLVED -- sf_pane_fingerprint() now strips digits, spinner glyphs, and drops the entire volatile status line wholesale before hashing, hand-traced correct against both the round-6 counterexample and the builder's new fixtures, and is now directly, non-tautologically unit-tested. FIND-031 (lock-steal only grep-tested) is RESOLVED -- hc_acquire_lock() is a real extracted function that hc_run() itself calls, and the new tests drive that exact function through acquire/refuse/steal scenarios against real filesystem state. Manual trace of the full self-fix.sh:38-56 branch and the loop-name normalization, restart-backoff, and output-staleness-escalation logic in healthcheck-lib.sh found no new logic defects, no permanent-disable path, and no success-without-real-side-effect path (RESULT is always written as RUNNING then SUCCESS/FAIL with 'real evidence' required by the fixer's own TASK text, and verify-loops.sh cross-checks the artifact independently via curl, never trusting the marker alone). The one remaining genuine gap is FIND-032 (major, not critical): the stateful decision branch that CONSUMES the now-correct fingerprint (self-fix.sh:38-56, specifically the age_min computation and the line-51 compound boolean) has zero test coverage of its own -- only the pure helper function it calls is tested. This is a real, non-cosmetic verification-readiness gap: a future regression in that branch (an inverted boolean, a units mistake in the age arithmetic, a broken PANEHASH read/write ordering) could silently make the 180-minute kill ceiling inert again, or conversely cause a genuinely-progressing fixer to be killed prematurely, and no test in this codebase would catch either regression. Because this is a genuine, concrete, file:line-cited MAJOR flaw directly bearing on the CLAIM's item (d) ('a hang that IS eventually killed'), overall verdict is FAIL, though narrower in scope than any prior round -- only verification_readiness fails, and it fails only on missing regression-test coverage for logic that was itself found correct by manual trace, not on a demonstrated bug.
